Title: Oxford Indoor Bouldering
Summary:
Hold on tight fellas (pun intended), OutdoorLads is now running a monthly indoor bouldering session in Oxford!
I'm sure many of us are no strangers to this kind of event, having become a very popular addition to ODL's catalogue with other chapters established in London, Bristol, Reading, Manchester and Sheffield.
For those new to the sport indoor bouldering is a form of rock climbing performed
without ropes or harness
on artificial walls (~3-4m) with crash mats underneath for safety. Here your technique and your problem solving ability counts just as much as your strength, so be prepared to work out both body and mind, all in a very social and friendly atmosphere (seriously, the puzzle solving nature of this sport acts as an amazing ice breaker when chatting to new people). I will also be there to welcome you into the group and answer any questions you may have, as well as offer climbing tips should you need them 😊.
We will be meeting at the
Gallery Bouldering
center located in the heart of Oxford, offering over 100m of bouldering wall (and growing) with a diverse range of routes catering for beginners all the way to Font 7C, so that there is something for all skill levels to enjoy. Afterwards we may also pop in for a pint at one of the many nearby pubs.
As with most climbing gyms there is a
waiver
that you will need to sign to check that you understand the risks involved and the proper climbing etiquette to follow to keep others and yourself safe while climbing. This can be filled out at reception but can also be done ahead of time by following the link
here
.
Please also note that this is a
liquid chalk only
gym, which can be readily purchased at reception.
Hope to see you there!
Difficulty & Distance: A range of climbs are available for all different skill levels to enjoy

Title: Lode up on Baildon Moor
Summary:
This circular journey through Bradford offers a mix of history and natural beauty.
We begin in Saltaire, a UNESCO World Heritage site and model village founded by Sir Titus Salt in 1853. A short walk through Roberts Park, with its Victorian features, sets the stage for our adventure.
Next, we walk along the historic Shipley Glen Tramway, dating back to 1895. The steep walk gives a glimpse into past leisure activities. Shipley Glen is an ancient glacial valley, with craggy outcrops, and is a favourite spot for hikers, horse riders, BMXers and climbers.
Climbing around 200m to Baildon Moor, we enjoy panoramic views and see Bronze Age markings. During the Industrial Revolution, the moor was vital for raw materials, evidenced by abandoned stone quarries.
We follow the moor down to Lode Pit Beck, with its rich mineral deposits. Taking a forest path along the Glen, we reach the River Aire. Our walk concludes by taking in Hirst Woods, an ancient woodland along the Leeds & Liverpool Canal and back to Saltaire.
There’ll be time after the walk for you to explore Saltaire village – from the architecture to Salts Mill (housing David Hockney exhibits, a bookshop & the Peace Museum - open until 5pm).
There’ll be an optional trip to a café, or grabbing a bite to take away from the village shops.
Dogs:
Well-behaved, socialised and under-control dogs are welcome on this event.
Dogs should be kept on a lead whenever this is signposted and whenever we are in the vicinity of livestock, and at the event leader's request.

Title: The Enchanted Forest Light Show
Summary:
By day, Faskally Forest near Pitlochry is a beautiful array of mixed woodland with some very tall trees indeed. It has lochans and a network of paths to entice you into the forest's depths.
For about 4 weeks a year, as the sun gets low in the sky, and when we put the clocks back, the forest is transformed by a mesmerising and interactive light show that blows your mind, "How have they come up with that?" It's not just about lights, it's about how they (a) mesmerise and (b) with narration educate about the importance of life in our forests for just about every other form of life on the planet.
WHEN?
OutdoorLads will be going on Sunday 1st November, 5.30pm. We're likely to be inside the forest for up to two hours. Clocks go back before then, sunset will be 4.30, so properly dark by 5.30.
WHAT'S THE PLAN?
Most importantly,
YOU HAVE TO PURCHASE YOUR OWN ENTRANCE TICKET
Signing up to the event page alone does not get you in. The ticket prices are about £40 but there are some concessions available.
Buy your ticket for Sunday 1st November, 17.30 slot. If this fills, you could buy for the slots either side and meet the rest of us inside.
The ticket includes coach travel from the centre of Pitlochry (close to the railway station) - you cannot gain access in your own vehicle. It includes the return of course.
WHAT ELSE MIGHT WE DO ON THE DAY?
Nearer the time, we'll see who's going and try to fix up a Sunday lunch for those who can get there early afternoon. Pitlochry is a lovely town with lots to see and do including local walks, shops, places to eat and drink.
If you're travelling by public transport, Pitlochry is well connected by rail and coach services with Ember, Citylink and Flixbus. Check engineering works that might affect Sunday and especially late Sunday trains.
This event is not suitable for dogs.

Title: BIRMINGHAM Indoor Climbing - MONDAY - Beginners
Summary:
Join OutdoorLads for an evening at Redpoint Birmingham Climbing Centre.
*** Beginner (supervised) events are not offered every week ***
If you have never climbed before (or need a refresher on the basics), then this BEGINNERS EVENT is ideal for you! We will happily show you the ropes & teach you everything you need to know to climb safely!
Event pages are split into
BEGINNER & EXPERIENCED.
Please ensure you sign up to the correct event as we can only supervise two beginners at once per leader.
This event is for beginner climbers (those needing to be supervised) only!
If you are competent with how to tie in & belay (safely & confidently), then you will need to
sign up to the accompanying experienced (independent climber) event
instead.
If you are climbing with us for the first time, whether Experienced or Beginner, it is essential that you send a note to the Event Leader telling them about your previous climbing experience & your goals!
Bouldering
- Most of us do roped climbing, but if you prefer to do bouldering, you can sign yourself in & go bouldering (unsupervised) instead of, or as well as, roped climbing. Please meet the leader & the group at the start though; some others might wish to do bouldering too!
Please note that we will not teach lead climbing or lead belaying on this event -
we would suggest having some
lessons in Lead Climbing
by a qualified member of staff if this is something you're interested in pursuing!
If you are subsequently unable to attend, please cancel off the event. Spaces for beginners are limited & 'no-shows' are not only rude, but also frustrating for the leader & other attendees who may have travelled over an hour away to climb with you!
Redpoint Birmingham Climbing Centre
Indoor climbing centres offer the challenges of climbing that you'll find on natural rock crags - simply indoors! It's a fun way to stay fit, make new friends & develop your climbing skills.
Climbing
- Unlike Indoor Bouldering there is a certain amount of skill to be mastered, such as tying in knots & belaying a partner, as well as the climbs being higher than in bouldering. If you are new to climbing (or would like a refresher), there are plenty of top-rope routes to choose from after learning the essential climbing & safety techniques with one of our friendly, experienced climbing leaders.
Bouldering
- Instead of tackling long high routes, the 'problems' (as they are referred to) are shorter & focus on technique, balance, body positioning & sometimes power. With the different emphasis, bouldering doesn't have the hassle of climbing with ropes, so it’s excellent (but not necessarily easier) for newcomers.
Redpoint Birmingham Climbing Centre
has more than 75 lines with over 300 routes, set through some spectacular ground including its notorious 'stalactite'. It even features one of the few indoor 'Yorkshire VS cracks' in the country, to test your jamming skills. The bouldering rooms are just as interesting as its climbing routes, over 200 bouldering problems have been organised into graded circuits to provide something for everyone.

Title: High Peak ‘in-steam’ Heritage Day Walk
Summary:
We will meet at Cromford Wharf Carpark, a short walk from Cromford Railway Station at 10.30am. I’ll be arriving at Cromford Mill, over the road from the carpark an hour beforehand so if you get in earlier they’ll be a chance to join me for a short tour.
A challenging walk taking in beautiful scenery, an abundance of wildlife, cracking views, and world renowned heritage, the Derwent Valley Mills having been awarded World Heritage Status in 2001. Cromford Canal is a haven for wildlife and a Site of Special Scientific Interest with little grebes and water voles, dragonflies, damselflies and hoverflies.
From Cromford Mill where there are a number of interesting buildings, we will follow the towpath from Cromford Wharf for one and a quarter miles to Leawood Pumping House.  The Pumping House was built in 1849 to pump water from the River Derwent into the canal, it operated for almost 100 years.
The walk has been planned to coincide with Heritage Open Days 2026 and a steaming day of two beam engines - Leawood Pumping Station and Middleton Top Engine House.
Experience the power of steam, the heat of the boilers, the smell of grease and coal and the power of the wave as tons of water are pumped...
Following this we will cross the canal walking between the old railway buildings of the High Peak Junction to ascend the steep High Peak Trail. At the foot of the incline is a catch pit, where runaway wagons once came to rest. On reaching the summit and Engine House we will be rewarded with views over the Derwent Valley. Remaining on the High Peak Trail we will aim to lunch at Black Rocks Visitor Centre (drinks and home-made cakes available here). Then onto Middleton Top where we will leave the Trail and walk though the historic limestone village of Middleton-by-Wirksworth before descending to meet the Via Gellia road and then onto Water Lane and Scarthin with views over Cromford Dam.
Those of you who would like to stay on might enjoy Arkwright’s Mill, Cromford village and/or a village pub to enjoy a well-earned pint or two before heading home.
All photos taken by Christopher Chambers, used with permission

Title: Breakfast and a Days Climbing in the Peaks
Summary:
Come and join OutdoorLads for breakfast and a days rock climbing at Windgather.
We'll start the day with a hearty breakfast at a great café in Chinley, just a few miles from the crag. It's a great way to support a local business while we plan our routes for the day.
Of course, if you're not a breakfast person, you're more than welcome to meet us at the crag car park at around 12:00.
Windgather Crag
is just a short walk from the roadside car park, around 5 km from Whaley Bridge, and is easily accessible from Sheffield, Manchester, Stoke-on-Trent, Macclesfield and Crewe. Chinley is also on the Manchester–Sheffield train line.
This event is suitable for all abilities and Beginners are especially Welcome!!
Never climbed outdoors before, or need a refresher? You're in the right place! Our leaders will show you the ropes, and you'll be climbing in no time. We'll set up several top ropes with bottom belays for everyone to use throughout the day, similar to what you'd find at an indoor climbing wall.
Climbing is a full-body workout. It's not just about strength; it also requires balance, problem-solving and planning. Outdoor climbing is a great way to stay fit, make new friends and enjoy the fresh air. This event will help you develop your climbing skills in a supportive environment.
For those who have climbed before (typically leading and lead-belaying indoors to around 6a) and want to develop their outdoor climbing, we'll have more experienced climbers for you to partner with. You'll be able to second routes and learn how to remove protection as you climb.
If you're an experienced climber with your own harness, helmet, rack and rope, we'll pair you with other competent climbers so you can choose and climb your own routes.
If you're not sure whether this event is right for you, just message the
event leader
, who'll be happy to answer any questions and help you decide.
As with any outdoor activity, we'll need to remain flexible depending on the weather, the availability of routes and the experience of everyone attending. The event may be adapted or, in exceptional circumstances, cancelled if weather conditions require, so please keep an eye on your messages in the days leading up to the event for any updates from the event leader.
Difficulty & Distance: Outdoor climbing for all abilities, but a moderate level of fitness is required.

Title: Eight Days a Week(end) of Fun: A Liverpool City Break
Summary:
*That sold quickly please join the waitlist as we are hoping to add a 3rd room which will increase our spaces by 6

Come and join us for a weekend break in Liverpool, and enjoy fun times exploring the city!
Liverpool is a vibrant maritime city in North West England, renowned as the birthplace of The Beatles, a powerhouse of football culture, and a hub of rich industrial history. Situated on the Mersey Estuary, it features UNESCO-listed docks, diverse cultural attractions, stunning architecture, and a lively, welcoming atmosphere. Liverpool is the most filmed city outside of London, recent productions filmed here include Batman, Captain America, Sherlock Holmes and Peaky Blinders.
City breaks are less formal and structured than our usual hostel breaks, you’ll have free time or time to do the suggested activities below, but they are all suggestions. City breaks do not have the usual Friday night buffet, (and indeed no food or drink is included in the price) however places to eat as a group will be suggested, or you may wish do your own thing or break into smaller groups.

Arrive late afternoon on Friday, meet & greet reception before heading off out for dinner and drinks. (Exact restaurant location to be confirmed nearer event date)

Saturday morning, Optional Breakfast at the hostel before we head out for a walking tour exploring the city's maritime heritage. We may stop for lunch at the Royal Albert Docks. If time we might take a trip on the
ferry across the Mersey!
In the afternoon there will be free time to explore the city with an optional visit to the
Beatles Museum
In the evening we will reconvene at the hostel before joining a local OutdoorLads social! Exploring the city's vibrant night life.
Day 3:
Sunday morning, Optional Breakfast at the hostel then free time before checkout - option of a visit to
Liverpool Cathedral
or the
Walker Art Gallery,
Or some adult crazy golf at
Golf Fang Liverpool

Hostel accommodation - 2 x  6 bed ensuite rooms which will only be shared with other OutdoorLads members attending the city break.
Please note that unlike most of our other hostel events, food is not provided and we will not have sole use of the hostel.

Title: Walk the wailing Wain Stones
Summary:
Total distance: about 18 km (approx. 11.2 miles), with 710 m (2325 feet) of ascent. Approximately 6 hours, including lunch. This walk includes some steep climbs and descents, as well as relatively flat sections (moorland). There is little shade for most of the walk, and given the elevation, it is usually windy.
Starting from the Clay Bank, we ascend towards the coast-to-coast path. This initial section takes us up above Hasty Bank (398 m) with magnificent views North, towards Middlesbrough and beyond. We then walk along a relatively flat stone path to the Wainstones.
The name "Wainstones" (a prominent sandstone outcrop on Hasty Bank in the North York Moors) is believed to originate from the ancient Anglo-Saxon word wanian, meaning to lament or grieve. Historically, the stones were called the "Stones of Lamentation", and legend suggests they may have been a burial site for a slain Danish chieftain. Another theory is that the jumbled, rock-strewn gap was simply viewed as a place to mourn or perform rituals. Alternatively, the name is sometimes linked to the archaic word "wain" (a poetic term for a wagon or cart), as the rocks' shape can vaguely resemble an old carriage from certain angles.
After a descent, and a short valley section, we are soon climbing again, this time towards Cold Moor (401 m). Despite the name, it was warm when I visited ;)
Continuing on, we climb above Carlton Bank to reach Cringle Moor before heading on to the Lord Stones.
The "
Lord Stones
" refer to a prominent collection of ancient boundary markers and prehistoric stones. The name originates from the Three Lords' Stone, which historically marked the point where the estates of three local lords met.
Bronze Age Barrow
: The primary stone sits atop the perimeter of an ancient Bronze Age burial mound. This area formed a small cemetery and ceremonial site thousands of years before the local estates were formed
We then reach
Lordstones cafe,
where refreshments can be bought. There are benches and a large flat area nearby, for those who bring a packed lunch.
After another more gradual ascent, we cross an exposed section of moorland. Our gradual descent takes us through a short section under trees. We then resume a gradual ascent towards Urra Moor. This section passes through an area where many partridges breed, so any dogs need to be kept under close control. We return to the path we started along earlier in the day, for a final 1.5 miles or so back to the car park.
For those who may like a drink after, the best local option is
The Dudley Arms
at Ingelby Greenhow, less than 3 miles away.
Dogs: Well-behaved, under control dogs are welcome at this event.
Dogs should be kept on a lead whenever signposted, whenever we are in the vicinity of livestock, and at the event leader's request. Many stretches of this walk include sheep roaming. I would also note that there are a few up-and-over wall stiles towards the end of the walk, so you get a bit of an upper-body workout lifting your dogs over them. You'll need to make sure you're carrying sufficient extra water for your four-legged friend. We do not encounter much natural water on this walk. If you're unsure, contact the leader for guidance.

Title: Sheffield Bouldering @ The Climbing Hanger
Summary:
Swap trainers for climbing shoes and join OutdoorLads for an evening of INDOOR BOULDERING at The Climbing Hanger in Sheffield.
Cards/contactless ONLY  - this venue does not accept cash
If you haven't been to The Hangar before, please click
here
to pre-register. Click on the link, scroll down, select Sheffield and follow the on-screen instructions. Completing the waiver prior to arrival will get you climbing faster.
What is Bouldering?
It's a form of climbing where instead of long high routes, the 'problems' tend to be shorter and focus on technique, balance, body positioning and sometimes power. Because of this different emphasis, bouldering doesn't have the hassle of climbing with ropes, harnesses and belaying, which makes it an excellent activity for newcomers to the sport. No wonder it's often regarded as the 'purest' form of climbing.
If you're a seasoned climber you won't need convincing about the benefits of bouldering, but for those who've never climbed more than a staircase, the benefits are wide ranging: from the physical - improved strength, tone, balance, power and coordination; mental - problem solving, focus, concentration and body awareness; to the emotional - relaxation, a sense of achievement and a feeling that mind and body are working together perfectly ('feeling psyched'). On top of all this, bouldering tends to be a very social sport where you can hang out with mates and each have a go as you feel regardless of what level you climb at.
I'm new to Bouldering - can I come along?
If you have never tried bouldering before it is recommended that you have a guided session from the event leader, who will go through everything you will need to know to boulder safely before joining in with the rest of the group.
I've been Bouldering before?
As above, everyone attending the event  must abide by the centre's T&Cs etc. As an experienced boulderer you responsible for your own safety, actions and involvement at all times. As such, you should use your own judgement in taking up advice given either by OutdoorLads Volunteers or other experienced climbers.
Photos : Copyright granted to OutdoorLads by the event leader / venue.
Please note that every person participating should be aware of (and accept) that those members perceived as ‘in charge’ or leading the event are not necessarily qualified, do not need to be qualified, and are not regarded by OutdoorLads, or themselves as ‘technical experts’ but are amateur climbers with some experience and who are happy to impart their knowledge. Any advice given should be considered with this in mind by the recipient.
All those attending the event must also be aware of the centre's own terms and conditions of participation and abide by them, along with any instructions given by the centre’s staff. Everyone must also take responsibility for their own safety while participating in Indoor climbing events.
Difficulty & Distance: Suitable for all abilities. If you're new to bouldering, just let the event leader know and we'll get you started!

Title: Durham Beer Festival '26 Social
Summary:
Join Craig and OutdoorLads for our next social event in Durham.
Durham is a beautiful cathedral and university city in North-East England. It is also home to
Durham Castle
, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Bill Bryson has called Durham ‘a perfect little city’, Condé Nast’s Traveller magazine readers voted it the ‘Best city in the UK’, and Which? members named it one of the UK's best city breaks for 2024. It is also the county town of County Durham. Durham is surrounded on three sides by a meander in the River Wear, with the surrounding land being hilly, except along the Wear's floodplain to the north and southeast.
The
Durham Beer Festival
(page currently still points to last year's event) is organised by
CAMRA
. They expect to have 30+ real ales and 8+ ciders and perries, selected from a wide range of independent national brewers.
Entry last year cost £5, which also included a half-pint glass and a programme. This page will be updated when more information becomes available.
Come and join us for a few drinks, find out about planned and forthcoming events, make new friends and catch up with people you have met before!
If you’re not familiar with Durham, it’s a wonderful city to explore on foot and make sure you include the cathedral.
All images provided by the event leader. OutdoorLads has permission to use them.

Title: The Tolkien Trail
Summary:
Join Mike and OutdoorLads for a 7 mile walk in the footsteps of J. R. R. Tolkien, famous author of ‘The Lord of the Rings’ trilogy and ‘The Hobbit’. We will cross farmland and some woodland and walk along the banks of the River Ribble and River Hodder. Points of interest include Stonyhurst College, where Tolkien is said to have spent a lot of time whilst writing the books, drawing inspiration from the surrounding areas. We will also pass the historic landmark, ‘Cromwell’s bridge’ on the River Hodder, named after Oliver Cromwell, who marched his army over the bridge in 1648 to fight in the Battle of Preston. This beautiful part of Lancashire is full of history, and with stunning views of Pendle Hill and the surrounding countryside, what more could you ask for?
We will stop for lunch at the midway point of our walk and, for those who wish to, there will be an opportunity to have a post-walk drink in one of the local establishments in Hurst Green.

Title: Roundhay Park - Autumn Walk
Summary:
Join Shaun and Mike for a relaxed 6.5km (4 miles) scenic autumn walk through one of Europe’s largest urban parks. Roundhay Park is a place where Leeds’ history, landscape, and culture all meet. From lakeside views and ornamental gardens to grand 18th‑century architecture and the echoes of world‑famous concerts.
We’ll set off from within the park and make our way around, visiting the folly built in the late 18th century as a summerhouse. This charming stone structure sits tucked above the lake and offers a glimpse into the park’s Georgian past. We’ll also see the Mansion, which overlooks sweeping lawns and remains a focal point within the park.
We’ll take our time, enjoy the scenery, and make the most of the park. There will be three opportunities for refreshments during the walk, so there’s no need to bring food, although you’re very welcome to do so.

on this walk.

Title: Yorkshire Dales Camp 2026
Summary:
Join OutdoorLads for a weekend in the beautiful Yorkshire Dales National Park in late Summer!
We will be camping in Upper Wharfedale, at the foot of Great Whernside.  Our location provides stunning views across the valley and opportunity for varied activities, including
walking, mountain biking and road cycling
. The main event on the Saturday will be a hike with wonderful views across the landscape - so it will involve a good climb! There may also be an easier low-level walk (subject to leader availability). On the Sunday there will most likely be a shorter and lower level walk on offer.
Our campsite is close to
Kettlewell Village
which has a range of facilities including three great pubs and an award-winning tearoom. There's even a traditional village store and an outdoor shop in case you forget that essential item. The campsite itself will be for the
exclusive use of OutdoorLads
, and has its own dedicated facilities, including free high quality hot showers, picnic benches and fire pit. The campsite allows BBQ'S but campfires that are ground based are not permitted. Fires raised off the floor and with protection for the grass underneath are permitted. There are a limited number of electric-hookups available which will be allocated on a first-come first served basis, if you want one of these then message the leader following event registration.
This is a compact site and we would encourage you to bring a smaller rather than a big party tent! You will not be able to park your car immediately next to your tent, but there should be room on site if people try to car share as far as possible.
Dogs:
Well behaved dogs are allowed but must be on the lead on the site, due to the proximity of livestock.
Caravans, Campervans, Motorhomes

Title: Glyder Fach & Glyder Fawr via Bristly Ridge (Scramble)
Summary:
Fancy a BIG day out in the mountains of Snowdonia / Eryri?
The Glyderau range sits just north of the Llanberis pass and the Snowdon range, and with summits similar in height to the mighty Snowdon / Yr Wyddfa it forms a worthy, interesting and far less crowded mountain experience. Our route up will take in one of the best
grade 1 scrambles
in the area -
Bristly Ridge
, a thrilling journey ‘off-path’ route which starts in the forebodingly named
Sinister Gully
and leads up onto the pinnacles that form the upper part of this fabulous 3 starred route.
Bristly Ridge is
challenging and exposed
in places, and although you don’t need technical rock climbing skills you will definitely need a head for heights, be sure footed and have
a sense of adventure
. This event is best suited to members who have scrambled confidently before, however if you are 'good' on your feet, physically fit with a head for heights and want to give it a go, I will be happy to have you join the team.
Having championed the challenge of the ridge we will then get to explore the summit of
Glyder Fawr
and visit the improbable rock monolith of the
Cantilever Stone
,  before heading over to
Castell y Gwynt
(Castle of the Winds). The top of the mountain is fractured into a myriad of angled lichenous covered slabs which make traversing the summit challenging fun in the dry and requiring carefully foot placement in the wet.  We will then head over to the summit of Glyder Fawr, which stands at a height of 1001 meters, before descending via
Devils Kitchen
to return to our start point.
Please note that the event may be liable to change or cancellation due to inclement weather.

Title: Bannau Brycheiniog Autumn Escape: The Brecon Peaks
Summary:
Join us for a fantastic autumn weekend away in the heart of the
Bannau Brycheiniog (Brecon Beacons)
We’ll be staying at a beautiful converted farmhouse surrounded by wooded slopes, rushing rivers, and dramatic peaks.
Whether you’re looking to conquer some serious mountain summits or enjoy a scenic, relaxed stroll along historic waterways, this weekend has something for everyone.
The hostel is a charmingly converted traditional Welsh farmhouse steeped in rustic character. It perfectly balances a remote, "getaway" vibe with modern comfort.
Historic Character:
The hostel retains its gorgeous original stonework, exposed timber beams, and a cozy lounge complete with a
wood-burning stove
—the ultimate spot to swap stories and unwind with the guys after a day on the trails.
Stunning Natural Setting:
Tucked away in a secluded valley just below the
Talybont Reservoir
, the hostel is surrounded by lush wooded slopes, cascading waterfalls, and rushing streams. You literally step out of the front door and directly onto the trails.
Dark Skies Oasis:
The area surrounding the hostel is a designated
International Dark Sky Reserve
. If the night is clear, you can take a five-minute stroll to the edge of the reservoir for breathtaking, unpolluted views of the constellations and the moon reflecting on the water.
The Weekend Plan
Friday: The Social Kick-off
Arrive from 4:30 PM and settle into our mountain home. We’ll kick things off with our traditional welcome buffet—a great chance to meet everyone and plot our adventures.
Note: Please bring a small contribution to share (enough for 2-3 people). Let’s keep it varied—creative salads, local meats, or snacks are great, but maybe let’s go easy on the quiche!
Saturday: The Main Event
We have two brilliant options for Saturday's walk, which will be finalised closer to the date depending on weather and group preference:
Option A: The Mountain High
– A classic, invigorating hike into the nearby Brecon Beacons peaks. Expect breathtaking ridges, stunning vistas, and a good workout.
Option B: The Canal Circuit
– A gentler but incredibly scenic circular walk tracking the historic Monmouthshire & Brecon Canal between Llangynidr and Talybont-on-Usk. Perfect for autumn colors, locks, and easy-going socializing.
Sunday: Morning Stretch & Depart
After breakfast, we'll pack up and check out. For those not rushing off, we can head out for a short local stroll or a pub lunch nearby before saying our goodbyes.
Food & Fuel
We’ve got you covered so you can focus on the views:
Included:
Breakfasts on Saturday and Sunday, plus a delicious group dinner on Saturday night.
Tea, Coffee & Cake:
Plenty provided throughout the weekend—because every hiker needs a sugar hit!
Your Part:
Just bring your Friday buffet contribution, your own preferred snacks/drinks, and a packed lunch for Saturday.
Dogs:
Sorry no dogs allow for this weekend (except registered assistance dogs - please let the office know
support@outdoorlads.com
when booking)

so come spend it with us in the Yorkshire Dales.
Family Christmas returns to Yorkshire, in one of the most welcoming spots we know! Join Chris and Mike for a festive three-nights in the Yorkshire Dales.
Whether you’re looking for a change from your usual plans or simply want somewhere to belong this year, we’ll be here to cook for you, laugh with you, and keep the festive spirit flowing. Expect chilled evenings in the lounge, maybe a movie night, a cheeky dance, terrible cracker jokes, and plenty of food.
With the Dales right outside the door, we’ll stretch our legs on Christmas Day and take a longer walk on Boxing Day, though you’re just as welcome to stay cosy inside with board games, chats, or a well‑earned nap.
Cheesy jumpers encouraged, Secret Santa guaranteed.
It’s the perfect way to spend the season — together, relaxed, and surrounded by the beauty of the Dales.
Accommodation
Our venue is a spacious independent hostel with a good size lounge and separate dining room, cosy conservatory area and a large kitchen together with bike store and a range of bedroom sizes. Outside, there's a large garden with beautiful views in every direction. If the weather is good there's a firepit, and a chance to relax around a fire. If not don't worry, we have the cosy hostel for comfort, relaxing chatting, board games etc.
There is no TV and while there is WiFi it can be patchy, so this hostel is a chance to socialise away from our screens!
There's a small but well stocked village shop a short walk away and provides all you may need, and there's a choice of excellent pubs in the village serving home cooked food (depending upon their Christmas opening times).
Food
Christmas Eve will be a buffet - bring an item for a one or two people to share but don't bring too much; we like to avoid too much wastage of food wherever possible. Dinner on Christmas day and Boxing day will be a shared meal cooked by the leaders, with breakfasts on all mornings included.

Title: Dolgellau Double 2: The Precipice Walk
Summary:
Route Description
The 4 mile Dolgellau Precipice Walk, as it is known locally, runs around the 12th Century Nannau estate and along the shore of Llyn Cynwch a working reservoir that provides Dolgellau with water. The path will take you through woodlands and meadows and then along a trail that clings to the edge of the hill (hence the name). Don't worry it isn't that scary! There are  captivating views of Yr Wddfa and the Moelwynion to the north, The Rhinogydd to the west, whilst Cader Idris, the Aran and Arenig ranges can be seen towards the south and east.
Although the path stands at 800ft above sea level, the starting point is already high up, so the route is relatively flat, and the reward factor vs effort expended is great. The route makes a good introduction to the area and is perfect to follow the more energetic route the day before. (see below)
After the circular route there is a hillfort on an adjacent hill to explore taking an hour or so. This part is 2 miles with 200m of height gain.  Those who prefer otherwise could be on their way home, or return to the town for tea and cake etc.
The Dolgellau Double
This event is one of 2 planned for this weekend in the area. Saturday's walk can be found at this link:
https://www.outdoorlads.com/events/dolgellau-double-1-beautiful-afon-mawddach-260912
.

and stay locally - for

which is handy for both walks, and also walking distance to the town with its many pubs and places to eat etc. - leave a message in the forum below and we can get together on site.  There are also bnbs 'gwestys' and hotels etc nearby, ranging from the basic to the most luxurious.

Title: Dolgellau Double 1: The beautiful Afon Mawddach
Summary:
Route Description
Our walk starts and ends in the charming and historic market town of Dolgellau (pronounced like Dol-geth-lie) which started life in the Welsh gold rush times, was famous for ship building and is now popular with hikers and climbers exploring the Cadair Idris mountain range that looms over the town. Our walk explores the land above the upper reaches of the stunning Mawddach Estuary.
Initially we will take a back lane out of the town to the small settlement of Llaneltyd where it joins with the Arfon Mawddach. We then ascend sharply up the side of Foel Ipris (328 m) to a level section on the hillside from where in good weather we will get some beautiful views down the estuary towards the coast, and of the Cadir Idris mountain range.
We descend back down through the forest and cross the river on a rustic and historic wooden toll bridge (charge
30 pence
–
please bring change
), to stop for a drink on the incredibly scenic terraces of the George III Hotel in Penmaenpool: Wales 'pub of the year'.
The last sector of the walk follows a disused railway which is now a well established cycle and walking route, and follows the Arfon Wnion back into the town. For those that wish to round off the day, Dolgellau has some great cafes and eateries.

Title: Fields, Woods & Wildlife: the Great Everdon Escapade
Summary:
This is a walk that may surprise anyone who is unfamiliar with this part of middle England; a beautiful 9-mile circular through the rolling hills of
South Northamptonshire
. Our walk takes in a selection of charming villages packed full of ironstone cottages, plenty of rural views, an enchanting wood and a stately home which now serves as a luxury country house hotel.
Starting on the village green in
Everdon
, we'll take the No Through Road up to the hamlet of
Little Everdon
, before cutting across the fields to
Newnham
. From there, we pick up the first mile or so of the
Nene Way
– a 110 mile path which starts in Northamptonshire and runs through Cambridgeshire and Lincolnshire all the way up to The Wash.
After skirting around
Badby
, we join the start of the
Knightley Way
– a scenic path that runs down to Towcester. One of the highlights of the walk takes us around the edge of Badby Wood – a
Site of Special Scientific Interest
and a haven for wildlife which has a history of continuous woodland cover for over seven hundred years.
Emerging from the wood, we cross over Badby Down to enjoy the first of a series of spectacular viewing spots where you can gaze at miles of unspoilt English countryside. We'll pause here for our picnic lunch, overlooking
Fawsley Hall
– a Grade I listed country hotel and spa.
Descending down past Fawsley and its tiny church which sits perched on a grassy knoll surrounded by a ha-ha to keep the cattle out, we cross the fields again and head up to the village of
Preston Capes
.
Here the gently undulating terrain becomes a little bit more challenging; after climbing up to Preston Capes and descending back down to the east of the village, we're in for a surprisingly steep climb back up to the corner of Mantles Heath. But the climb is well worth it – we're rewarded with more spectacular views looking northwards towards Daventry and Warwickshire beyond.
Having caught our breath, it's back down into the valley and across the fields to return to Everdon and an opportunity to quench our thirst at
The Plough Inn
.
Dogs are welcome:
Our walk includes some short stretches on country roads and village streets. We may encounter sheep, lambs, cows or horses and there are a few fields where landowner signs request dogs on a lead.

Title: Fireside evenings above the Calder Valley
Summary:
A weekend retreat to remember!
Perched high above the Calder Valley, this 17th‑century Grade II listed camping barn has a real off‑the‑beaten‑track feel, surrounded by open countryside and wide Pennine views. It’s a perfect place to experience the autumn leaves and the breezes that sweep across the rolling hills.
From the barn, there are many options for nearby walks include the dramatic ridge to Stoodley Pike, loops around local reservoirs, or gentler valley walks towards Hebden Bridge and Hardcastle Crags. For those wanting something lower level, there are plenty of scenic paths straight from the door. If you’re not walking, you can head into Todmorden or Hebden Bridge for cafés, shops and a slower day, or settle in for a reading day in the large indoor activity space.
This event is a two‑night weekend retreat. Walks will take place on Saturday, with routes chosen closer to the time based on weather. It’s also a great opportunity to get involved in route planning if you’d like to contribute.
Accommodation
The barn is simple, but we’ll create fantastic memories through community, conversation and cosy fireside moments. This peaceful rural setting is a great way to experience the wilder side of West Yorkshire. Expect a couple of days of walking, cooking together and being part of a friendly, welcoming group.
There are three bunk‑bed rooms sleeping 8, 10 and 12 people, plus a fourth accessible room. No bedding is provided – you MUST bring your own sleeping bag, bedding and pillow.
We’ve got access to a well‑equipped kitchen with fridge/freezer, a lounge area, an accessible wet‑room shower, toilet blocks, and a large indoor barn space for activities. Wi‑Fi is available.
Heating is provided by wood‑pellet and multifuel stoves, and there’s also an outdoor fire pit and campfire area for relaxed evenings.
Food
Friday night will be a buffet – please bring something to share. Saturday night will be a shared meal cooked by the leader, with breakfast included on both Saturday and Sunday mornings.

This event is not suitable for dogs.

Title: Glentress Long Weekend
Summary:
Come and join our friends at OutMTB for a long weekend of off-road biking fun at Scotlands premier mountain biking centre.
Glentress itself is a huge trail centre, with a mixture of more traditional forest trails with lots of fun, techy features and plenty of newer, faster-flow trails.  Nearby Innerleithen also has some fantastic official trails and there are also some smashing natural trails.  The plan for the weekend is to combine some of all of these elements, although plans might change a little when we see what the weather brings!
Please note: OutMTB is aimed at the full LGBT community, so there is a chance that there may be members of other genders on this event.
This is a mountain biking trip, so a well serviced mountain bike will be required - front suspension minimum.
Current plans are:
Saturday 29th - Glentress trails.  Intermediate level ride, mixture of blue and red trails.  Likely around 25km, 800m elevation, 2-4 hours riding.
Sunday 30th - Gypsy Glen.  This is a nearby route of natural MTB trails.  This means fewer features like berms and jumps, but more unpredictable things like rocks and roots.  Comes with some excellent views!  This is also an intermediate type ride, 2-4 hours duration, 25km distance and 700m of elevation.
Sunday 31st - Innerleithen red trails: again 2-4 hours riding, 25km and around 800m elevation.
We will meet at the Glentress carpark for the Saturday event.  Should you wish to only attend the Sunday/Monday then get in touch and we will arrange a meeting point.
There are lots of accommodation options in the area.  I will be sharing a lodge at Glentress, there are also pods and camping spots and the lower part of the area, as well as plenty of hotel options either at Glentress or nearby Peebles. Bike hire is available at Glentress.

Title: Manchester Pride 2026 - Grindr: The Opera!
Summary:
Join us as we celebrate and promote
OutdoorLads
at one of the UK’s biggest and best Pride events!
🏳️‍🌈
Grindr: The Opera! puts the most notorious gay hook-up app into the exaggerated world of opera. This musical parody takes you on a hilarious and thought-provoking journey through the world of gay dating, focusing on the greatest catalyst for the shift: GRINDR.
With catchy songs, witty dialogue, and colourful characters, this unique and ground-breaking production explores the impact of technology on human connection and the search for meaningful relationships.
Through the experiences of four gay men who use Grindr to connect with each other,
Grindr: The Opera!
offers a satirical commentary on modern gay culture.
Devon the romantic, Tom the cynic, Jack the twink and Don the daddy meet via the medium of the Grindr app, each seeking a different type of connection.
You’ll laugh, you’ll cry, and you’ll be challenged to think deeply about the ways in which technology is shaping our lives and relationships.
But above all,
Grindr: The Opera!
will make you feel alive. With its infectious energy, dynamic performances, and unforgettable characters, this production will leave you feeling inspired, entertained, and maybe even a little bit hopeful about the future of human connection.

Title: Manchester Pride 2026 - The Vigil
Summary:
Join
OutdoorLads
as we come together for one of the most moving and meaningful moments of the Manchester Pride weekend — the
Candlelit Vigil
in Sackville Gardens.
We’ll be meeting at
The Molly House from 7:30pm
, giving us time to socialise and catch-up before walking together to
Sackville Gardens by 8:30pm
for the start of the vigil.
This event is
open to all
, and you do
not
need a Manchester Pride wristband to attend.
🕯️ About the Candlelit Vigil
Hosted in partnership with George House Trust
, which has supported people living with HIV since 1985, the vigil is a powerful evening of remembrance, reflection and unity.
As the sun sets and Sackville Gardens is illuminated by candlelight, we stand together in silence to remember those we have lost to HIV and other causes, and to show support for those who continue to suffer or face persecution simply for being who they are.
This is a space for solidarity, hope and healing – a moment to reaffirm our commitment to inclusion, visibility and compassion for our LGBTQ+ siblings across the world.
Candles will be available in the gardens for a small donation to George House Trust
, who help organise and host this incredibly special event.
Whether this is your first Manchester Pride or you’ve attended many times before, the vigil offers a moment of calm and connection to close the weekend with purpose.
We hope you can join us.

Once again, we’ll be right in the heart of the action,
outside Via in the Gay Village

Title: Manchester Pride 2026 - The Parade!
Summary:
Join us as we celebrate and promote
OutdoorLads
at one of the UK’s biggest and best Pride events!
🏳️‍🌈
We’re back with a bang this year! To celebrate 20 incredible years of OutdoorLads, we’re levelling up - we’ll have both a
float and a group of walkers
following behind as we march through the city. Expect the same high energy, bold spirit, and pride as we mark two decades of community, adventure, and friendship.
💚 The Theme:
No Place Like Home
This year, Manchester Pride celebrates the theme "No Place Like Home." For many of us, our community is the home we found for ourselves - a place of belonging, safety, and authentic connection.
OutdoorLads has been that home for thousands of people over the last 20 years, providing a space where we can be exactly who we are. Join us - whether on the float or as part of our walking contingent—as we take to the streets of Manchester to celebrate our history, our chosen family, and the unique spirit that makes our community feel like home.
📍 The Plan
We'll gather at the meeting point (Location & Time TBC) please keep an eye on your messages and this event page as this is how we'll provide updates closer to the day. We’ll be easy to spot, just look for the red OutdoorLads T-shirts (which you’ll need to wear!).
As always, we want to showcase everything that makes OutdoorLads awesome, so if you're able, get involved by bringing gear that reflects your favourite activities:
Climbers
– Wear your harness. Bonus points for clipping on nuts, hexes or cams for a bit of jingly flair!
Cyclists / Mountain Bikers
– Ride along-side on your bike. Bells and horns encouraged for extra fun!
Walkers / Hikers
– Walking poles, rucksacks, hydration bladders (contents at your discretion!) and massive OS maps are all welcome. Bonus points if you act lost and ask the crowd for directions.
We’ll also have
flags to wave
,
stickers to hand out
, and heaps of enthusiasm to share!
Most importantly, don’t forget your red OutdoorLads T-shirt!
🎟️ Parade Wristbands
To take part in the parade, you
must
collect a wristband from our muster point.
No wristband = no parade entry.
Please arrive on time, as late arrivals last year struggled to get one.
🚫
Please note:
Dogs are not allowed in the parade. This is a restriction set by the parade organisers.
🌈 After the Parade
We’ll be spending time in the Village after the parade, both to socialise and to represent OutdoorLads to potential new members.
We'll likely break into small groups to chat to the public, hand out stickers and encourage sign-ups (ideally while enjoying a few drinks in the sunshine!).
📍 Details of where to meet after the parade will be announced on the day.
Important:
You’ll need a separate
Manchester Village Pride
ticket
to access the Village after the parade. Tickets for the Gay Village Party purchased
here
.
The
parade wristband does not
grant access to the Pride event, so we recommend getting your event wristbands in advance if you plan to join us in the Village afterwards.
More details will be added here and emailed to participants as plans develop. It’s going to be another fantastic year.
We can’t wait to see you there!
🎉

Title: Manchester Pride 2026 - Picnic in the Park
Summary:
Join OutdoorLads for a picnic in the park to celebrate Manchester Pride!
We’re back!
After the fantastic success of our
2025 Picnic in the Park
, we’re thrilled to bring this event back for
Manchester Pride 2026
!
This is a fantastic opportunity to
meet new faces
,
catch up with old friends
, and ease into the celebrations before heading into the Village for the evening.
🧺 What to Bring
Your favourite picnic snacks and drinks (alcohol is allowed as the event is outside the Village cordon)
A blanket to sit on
Pride flags, face glitter, or anything else to get into the spirit!
OutdoorLads red T-shirt if you want to stand out in the crowd
No schedule or pressure – just turn up when you can and stay for as long as you like.
📍 Location
Vimto Gardens
is a peaceful green space just a few minutes' walk from both
Sackville Gardens
and the
Gay Village
. It's an ideal spot to gather before the festivities kick off.
We’ll be easy to find with our red shirts, pride flags, and picnic gear. Just look for the OutdoorLads gathering in the park!
This is a wonderful, low-key way to start your weekend, whether you’re arriving in Manchester on the Friday or just looking to enjoy some downtime with fellow OutdoorLads members before heading into the Village. No wristband required to join us for the picnic, so it’s completely open to anyone who wants to join!
We can’t wait to see you there and make more memories together at this returning favourite event!

Title: BIG20: BIG Wye Weekender (Hostel)
Summary:
The wait is finally over and we're ready to tell you all about our new BIG Event ... and it's a BIG20 event where we will be celebrating fabulous 20 years of OutdoorLads!
Nestled along one of the UK’s most scenic rivers, the Wye Valley is a haven for outdoor enthusiasts seeking both adventure and tranquillity. With its dramatic limestone cliffs, ancient woodlands, and winding river views, the area offers a breath-taking backdrop for everything from exhilarating climbs to peaceful walks. Whether you’re hiking along panoramic ridge trails, cycling quiet country lanes, or gliding through the valley by kayak, the Wye Valley delivers an unforgettable connection with nature.
Our location for the weekend is just as picturesque, a Georgian Farmhouse perched on the top a hill overlooking the surrounding valleys, which has been converted into a Outdoor Education centre and recently brought back into community ownership, the site is all ours for the Bank Holiday Weekend.

Title: Late summer camping in the beautiful Meon Valley
Summary:
Celebrate the end of the summer camping season in the Moen Valley, near the western edge of the South Downs.  We will be on the grounds of the Bereleigh Estate, which is the home to the Tyrwhitt-Drake family.
Campsite facilities include full shower blocks, washing up areas and they are dog-friendly (£4.00 per dog per night).  Campfires are allowed so there will be 'smores!!!  The site cannot accommodate caravans, but campervans are allowed; however there are no electric hook-ups.
Friday Afternoon:
Arrive any time after 13.30, look for the ODL flag and gazebo, pitch up, and settle in.  We will be in the Paddock Camping Area, and when we you arrive, we will simply text the Reception team and they will check us in.  Dinner this evening can be around the tents or at The Dell, which is the on-site cafe, with pizzas (best ordered in advance - more on that later!) and paninis.
Saturday morning:
Should the weather cooperate, the plan is to venture out on this 8.5 mile hike to
East Moen Stone Bridge
, with a potential stop at
Ye Olde George Inn
before heading back to the campground.  Lunch will need to be brought along, or there may be some offerings at the local off-license in East Moen.
Saturday Evening
After unwinding back at the campground, dinner can again be cooked around the tents or at
The Dell
.  If we are feeling adventurous, we could head back to Ye Olde George.
Sunday
If the weather is decent, breakfast can be a bit relaxed but we need to be off site by midday.
New to Camping ?
If this is your first event, don't be put off if you lack some of the necessary equipment; just message me on
chris.keivit@outdoorlads.com
or on Telegram -
@chriskk_fafner
.
Campfires & BBQ's
: This event may include a campfire/BBQ at the site.  Whilst our event leaders will take safety precautions there is still a risk to members. Please consider your behaviour around the campfire for your own and others safety.
Food and drink
: In addition to the offerings at the site, the nearest grocery stores are Aldi, Lidl, M&S, Tesco and Waitrose in Petersfield (if you are coming from the north / northeast).  If arriving from the Winchester direction, all the major stores are there, as well as a Tesco Express and Coop in New Alresford.
Dogs:
The site is dog friendly (kept on the leads), but at a cost of £4.00, payable locally.
Photos:
All photos have been provided by OutdoorLads members and used with permission and thanks.
Difficulty & Distance: A late summer campsite with a Saturday walk

Title: Mountain Walk Leaders Training Weekend
Summary:
Note:
This event is for existing mountain walk leaders and those who have booked their mountain walk leader assessment only. Please only sign up if you fall into one of those two categories.
The purpose of this event is for mountain walk leaders to get together for a weekend of peer-to-peer training, exchange of ideas and discuss experiences leading walks in the mountains. The event is heavily subsidised by OutdoorLads, to support leader training and development.
Over the weekend, we'll aim to get out in the local hills and practice some mountain skills. These could include:
Navigation in poor visibility
Route choice on difficult and steep terrain
Managing groups (in poor weather or with differing abilities etc.)
Assisting unconfident walkers on steep exposed terrain
The exact topics we'll cover can be decided over the weekend depending on what everyone wants to cover.
We'll be staying in the Fylde Mountaineering Hut (Little Langdale Cottage) on the Friday and Saturday night. Breakfasts and Saturday evening meal will be included, with the Friday evening meal being the usual ODL buffet.
Dogs

Title: Dartmoor Circular: Forests, Tors, and Ancient Stones
Summary:
Join us for a spectacular, varied circular day hike right through the atmospheric heart of northeastern Dartmoor. This route truly has a bit of everything: rushing rivers, deep evergreen forests, exposed ridge lines, stunning panoramic tors, and some of the finest prehistoric monuments the moor has to offer.
Setting out from near the iconic Warren House Inn, we’ll start by dropping south towards the peaceful valley of Soussons Down, winding through the trees before looping west past historic farmsteads towards Postbridge. Here, we'll cross the East Dart River near its famous ancient clapper bridge.
From Postbridge, we begin our steady northward march along the edge of the open moorland, tracking beneath Hartland Tor and Stannon Tor, with wide-open views expanding out to the west. We'll climb up towards Grey Wethers—the striking twin bronze-age stone circles nestled right on the edge of the woods.
Our route then takes a scenic, sheltered turn into the pine-scented tracks of Fernworthy Forest, skirting the southern edge of the beautiful Fernworthy Reservoir. After a quick stop to admire the water and the nearby hut circles, we’ll break back out onto the open moor via Chagford Common and Hurston Ridge. Our final stretch carries us south along the ridge line, enjoying commanding views of the landscape before returning to Warren House Inn for a well-earned drink.

Title: Icknield Way: Pegsdon Hills
Summary:
Join Alex for this slightly longer 14-mile Chiltern circular walk via the Icknield Way.
We will begin in the Hertfordshire town of Hitchin and our route will take us south out of the the town centre. Here we will turn west and follow the Chiltern Way into undulating countryside and ascend the beginnings of the Chiltern escarpment as we approach the village of Great Offley, named after the Mercian King Offa. After leaving the village we will turn north, passing the the 12th-century church of Mary Magdalene, and head out into open fields for another couple of miles.
Shortly after crossing into Bedfordshire we will reach the Pegsdon Hills, with wide-ranging views to the north. We may see some Highland cattle grazing as we join the the Icknield Way and follow it the along ridge of the hills towards the trig point at Deacon Hill. Our route will descend sharply before we head into woodland, passing by the edge of the Knocking Hoe nature reserve which also has good views of the surrounding farmland and villages.
Continuing on the Icknield Way we will head east towards the pleasant village of Pirton where the parish church of St Mary sits beside the remaining earthworks of a castle. From here we will walk back towards Hitchin, entering the town via the Oughtonhead nature reserve with its herd of English longhorn cattle. We will pass through the town centre, via Market Place and another St Mary's church, before heading back towards the station.

Title: Halloween at Dunster: Castles, Coast, and Celtic Hills
Summary:
Join us for a fantastic, varied Halloween day walk exploring the dramatic landscapes surrounding the historic medieval village of Dunster. This is a relatively short, circular route packed with diverse scenery—taking us from ancient wooded hills and historic settlements to the sweeping Somerset coastline, before tracking the nostalgic West Somerset Railway.
We’ll finish with plenty of time to spare in the afternoon to explore the magnificent Dunster Castle and its gorgeous gardens. Costumes are entirely optional, but a bit of Halloween spirit is highly encouraged!
Event Overview
Date:
Saturday, 31st October 2026
Duration:
Approximately 4 hours (excluding castle visit)
Distance:
Around 8.5 miles (13.5 km)
Difficulty:
Moderate. A few steady climbs into the hills, but well-paced with plenty of flat coastal walking to balance it out.
The Route
We begin our journey in the shadow of Dunster Castle, heading straight out into the atmospheric autumnal canopy of Dunster Park.
The Highs:
We’ll climb steadily up through the woods towards the ancient iron-age hillforts of
Bat’s Castle
and
Black Ball
, offering spectacular, moody views over the surrounding Somerset landscape and the Bristol Channel.
The Valleys & Villages:
Skirting the ridges of Aller Hill and Withycombe Hill, we'll drop down through the quiet combes and charming villages of Withycombe and Carhampton.
The Coast:
From Carhampton, we head north to meet the coast at
Blue Anchor
. Here, we'll grab some fresh sea air and look out across the waves.
The Rails:
The final leg brings us back west, tracking alongside the historic
West Somerset Railway
line and crossing the flat marshlands straight back into Dunster.
Afternoon: Dunster Castle & Gardens
After wrapping up the walk, the afternoon is yours to enjoy. We will head over to Dunster Castle (managed by the National Trust). Perched dramatically on a tor, this ancient fortress turned grand country house is the perfect setting for a Halloween afternoon.
You can wander through the multi-tiered subtropical gardens, explore the historic mill, or head inside the castle to soak up centuries of history (and perhaps a ghost story or two).
> Note: National Trust members get into the castle and gardens for free, so remember to bring your membership card! Non-members can purchase tickets on the day.
A Few Haunted Highlights... 🕷️
Dunster has a reputation for being one of the most active paranormal hotspots in the country—local lore says nearly every historic building in the village has a resident spirit. The castle itself has been investigated by the National Trust for its eerie occurrences. Keep an eye out for:
The Grey Lady:
Dunster’s most famous resident spectre, she is frequently seen gliding majestically down the grand 17th-century oak staircase before completely vanishing into a solid wall.
The Man in Green:
If you pop into the National Trust gift shop (housed in the old 17th-century stable block), you might spot a mysterious figure dressed head-to-toe in green walking calmly through the building before disappearing into thin air.
The Chinking of Coins:
On certain days, the ghostly sound of money being counted echoes near the old keeps. Local legend attributes this to the infamous William de Mohun ("The Scourge of the West"), who minted his own illegal currency here during the medieval Civil War.
The Foot of the Blue Kitchen:
In one of the modernised volunteer areas known as the Blue Kitchen, a shaken worker once reported a completely disembodied, naked human foot appearing out of nowhere on the floor before dissolving.
The Seven-Foot Skeleton:
Deep beneath the Gatehouse dungeon, archaeologists once uncovered the remains of a prisoner standing over seven feet tall, still shackled by his wrists and ankles to the stone wall. While no specific ghost has been spotted, visitors note a distinct drop in temperature, and dogs notoriously refuse to go near the steps leading down to it.
Even on our walk before we reach the castle, keep your ears open—tourists on the nearby hills have previously reported the distinct, booming sound of a massive troop of soldiers marching past them, despite the hillsides being completely empty!
What to Bring
Footwear:
Sturdy walking boots or muddy-trail shoes are highly recommended, as the woodland and hill paths can be damp and slick in late October.
Clothing:
Layer up for autumn weather and bring a reliable waterproof jacket—the coastal stretch can get breezy!
Food & Drink:
Pack a packed lunch, snacks, and plenty of water for the trail. We will find a scenic spot along the hills or coast for a lunch stop.
Money/Card:
For entry to the Castle/Gardens if you aren't an NT member, or for a well-deserved hot drink/pint in Dunster afterwards.

Keeping Dogs Under Effective Control)

Title: Yorkshire Three Peaks Hostel 2026
Summary:
Join OutdoorLads for an early September hostel break to walk the
Yorkshire Three Peaks!
You've probably heard of the National Three Peaks of Ben Nevis, Snowdon/Yr Wyddfa and Scafell Pike, in many ways more a driving challenge than a walking challenge, and requiring a certain level of insomnia.
But did you know there is also a famous walking challenge in Yorkshire too, walking (approximately) a marathon
over a circuit of Whernside, Ingleborough and Pen y Ghent in the Dales?  It's that challenge we will be undertaking on this hostel weekend, with the added benefit of a comfortable lounge to sit in and a proper (bunk) bed to sleep in afterwards!
Why not do some other OutdoorLads mountain walks to get your fitness up before tackling the challenge?
Don't worry, though, if it turns out you can't make it all the way round, the route takes us past Horton-in-Ribblesdale station where it would be possible to take a train back to Ribblehead, and it'd be possible to bail off after our first mountain, Whernside, and head for the pub.  So if you think you can do it and fancy a go please do sign up!
The Plan
Friday evening
: arrive from 4:30pm (no earlier please), we will have the traditional OutdoorLads buffet and a briefing around 8pm before socialising at the hostel or maybe a visit to the local pub.
Saturday
: we will be up quite early to head out after breakfast onto the main event, the Yorkshire Three Peaks walk, with the aim being to complete it within 12 hours if possible.  When we get back we'll have tea/coffee and cake, and a hearty dinner which I'm sure we will all need by then, then we can socialise in the hostel, pop out to the pub or if you're really worn out maybe an early night - or perhaps bring your favourite board game if that's your thing?
Sunday
: after breakfast it'll be time to pack, sort out the hostel and say our goodbyes.  I don't plan as things stand to offer a Sunday walk (we'll all be tired!) but you might want to do some touristing around the local area before heading home?
Sponsorship?
Unlike the Keswick to Barrow walk which OutdoorLads also takes part in as a fundraiser, this isn't specifically being run as a sponsored event, but if you fancy doing some fundraising yourself as part of this walk, either for OutdoorLads or for another charity of your choice, please feel free (and thanks in advance if you do decide to support OutdoorLads!)
Other Activities
While the main intention of this hostel is to complete the Three Peaks of Yorkshire walk, if other mountain or lowland leaders join the event it may be possible to offer shorter walks as well.  If you are such a leader, please send me a message via my profile below to let me know what you are interested in offering and I will note it on here.  Thank you :)
It would also be possible to stay with us in the hostel and do your own thing if you're a cyclist or just want to "train geek out" and have a ride on the scenic Settle-Carlisle Line (the town of Settle is said to be a nice day out, as is the city of Carlisle), take some photos of the famous Ribblehead Viaduct, have a meal and a pint at the Station Inn or just chill at the hostel!  If this is your intention please send me a message when you've booked on so I know I don't need to account for you on the main walk.
Dogs
Regrettably this event is not suitable for dogs - the walk is probably too long for most and they are not allowed in the hostel by the owners.  Sorry!

Title: See Loch Ness From Above
Summary:
Probably the most famous stretch of water in the world.
If you've not yet seen the beloved Nessie, maybe viewing her home from above will improve your chances!! If you don't know what to look for, shots of Nessie and her offspring are included in the photos on this page......
Loch Ness, as well as being home to Nessie, has a few other impressive facts about it (yes, Nessie's residence in the Loch is a fact!!) Loch Ness contains more water that all the rivers and lakes of England combined. It is far deeper than almost any part of the vast North Sea.
Enough marketing, let's get on with our day out.
We'll be seeing Loch Ness from above by climbing up a lovely hill called Meall Fuar-mhonaidh. That's easy for you to say. It stands proud at 699m above sea level.
The walk is out and back, 9km / 6miles and takes in some beautiful woodland before ascending slopes on open hillside. There are a few short, steep sections, but nothing of any real challenge. The walk is suitable for any reasonably active hill walker.
From the summit, if conditions allow, we should be able to see almost the full length of Loch Ness, with just a litre or two towards Inverness obscured by the hills. In the other direction, way beyond Loch Ness in the Great Glen, we should see Ben Nevis towering above Fort William. In other directions, we get a glimpse of seemingly endless summits in the Highlands. Finally, with a stroke of luck, we might see Nessie in her waters or sunning herself on a remote lochside beach.
Dogs are welcome on this walk, kept under close control.

Title: Hereford and Breinton Springs
Summary:
Join Alex for a slow and largely flat 10km / 6 mile walk from Hereford Cathedral to the National Trust site of
Breinton Springs
.
This short walk starts and finishes in the cathedral grounds in Hereford and takes a leisurely stroll along the river Wye.
Along the way you get some stunning views of the cathedral and the river before ending up in a peaceful churchyard surrounded by ancient orchards and the possibility of coming face to face with some endangered wildlife in an SSSI. We also walk past the spot where a dog fell into the Wye more than a hundred years ago, inspiring Elgar to write one of the
Enigma Variations
. On our return to the city we take a loop through the site where
Hereford Castle
once stood.
The walk is planned for the end of September, so if you wished to stay in Hereford until the following day, you could join the
Queers & Beers monthly meet up
, which normally takes place on the last Sunday of the month. And if you were to arrive early, you could pop to the café in All Saints Church to check out a
particularly rude wood carving
.

Title: Midweek Meander - Iron Giant Meatballs
Summary:
Join Alex for a slow walk in Derbyshire, taking in the Iron Giant and ending up in the IKEA restaurant.
The Bennerley Viaduct, known informally as the Iron Giant, and occasionally described as
Derbyshire's Eiffel Tower
is a wrought iron structure that once carried a railway. It proved impossible to demolish, got listed in the 1970s and recently has been cared for by a friends group who have worked hard to get a decent footpath over the top of it.
IKEA
opened in Nottinghamshire in 1997
and revolutionised home furnishings in the East Midlands. Their low priced café is where we will finish our walk and while they are most famous for their meatballs, their menu includes veggie options. Signing up for an
IKEA Family card
in advance might give you a deal in the restaurant.
This walk includes a Nottinghamshire furniture giant and Derbyshire iron giant. The boundary between the two counties is the River Erewash which we will cross.

Title: New Date: Wind In The Willows River Summer 😎 Sunday Saunter
Summary:
Walk Rescheduled From Sunday 12th July To Sunday 23rd Aug Due To Prolonged Heatwave Conditions.
Join us for a relaxed and sociable 10-mile circular walk through some of the most quintessentially English stretches of the Thames Valley – with one cheeky hill to earn your lunch. This is classic
“Wind in the Willows” country
. The Wind in the Willows was inspired by this very stretch of river, where Kenneth Grahame spent part of his childhood in Cookham. As we walk beside the Thames, it’s not hard to imagine Ratty and Mole “messing about in boats” along these same waters. Think lazy riverbanks, boats drifting by, and just enough charm to make you feel like you should be carrying a picnic hamper (or at least a decent snack).
The route is 10 miles, however there is the option just to do the morning section (just over 5 miles) and take the train back from Marlow Station.
The Route:
Starting at Cookham Station, we will initially walk into the older centre of the village, past the Stanley Spencer Gallery. We will then walk through the churchyard of the scenic Holy Trinity Church and then join the Thames Path, following the river for about 1.5 miles.
Later we will diverge from the Thames Path walking uphill towards Winter Hill where we are rewarded with sweeping views across the Thames Valley. We will follow the ridge for some time before climbing back down and then taking a flatter route towards Marlow. Entering Marlow, we will walk over it's historic bridge (see more details below) before getting to it's lively High Street.
At lunch we will take an extended break enabling participants to do their own thing, whether grabbing a coffee and sandwich in one of the cafes or a picnic lunch in the riverside park.
After lunch we will re-join the Thames path, which is now on the North side of the river, and walk along it for 3 miles towards Bourne End with it's marina. At the railway bridge we cross back to the South side of the river, re-trace some of our steps from the morning walk and then take a path back towards Cookham Station following the railway line across fields and later passing by a golf course.
Depending on the time that we arrive back, mindful that for those taking the train services are just hourly, there may be time for a quick drink or tea and cake at the nearby cafe (which closes at 4pm on Sundays).
The Sites:
Cookham:
is a quintessential Thames-side village, widely regarded as one of the most picturesque in England. The village has a strong artistic identity, most notably through its association with Stanley Spencer, whose work vividly depicted local life; and his legacy is preserved in the Stanley Spencer Gallery.
Winter Hill:
located just above Cookham, is characterised by its elevated position and sweeping views across the Thames Valley and the Chilterns. Much if it is protected by the National trust.
Marlow:
is a lively and attractive Georgian town that blends historic character with a strong leisure and dining scene. The town’s elegant suspension bridge, designed by William Tierney Clark, is a notable landmark and the famous Chain Bridge in Budapest, designed by the same architect, is a larger scale replica of Marlow Bridge.
Bourne End:
is a village where the Thames meets the River Wye and has a marina and railway bridge which we will pass and cross. The area also played a role in early British film production at Riverside Studios.

Title: Northern Ireland's Causeway Coast
Summary:
We're off over the Irish Sea for four nights to explore the Causeway Coast.
Our hostel has a sea view and is in an ideal location for seeing the various attractions of the area - top of the list is the Causeway Coast itself with its hexagonal basalt columns, this being part of a fine coastal walk. Also within walking distance of the hostel is Carrick-a-Rede rope bridge, perhaps not for those with a fear of heights as it hangs 30m above the sea!
A short drive away is Ballycastle with the historic Bonamargy Friary and it's harbour, this being the port for the short sailing to Rathlin Island - an island six miles long with tranquil walking trails and views back across the causeway coast. If we go a little further east we find ourselves in the Glens of Antrim, an area of ancient woodlands and waterfalls with several beautiful walking trails.
There is lots more to see and do, but why not just come along and discover this stunning part of Northern Ireland....
Our hostel has lots of social space, free table tennis & pool and clean, comfortable dorm rooms - plus a pub 100m away. It's absolutely perfect as a base to explore the local area and this stunning coastline.

Title: Gran Canaria Adventure Week 2027
Summary:
The last four years have proven to be hugely successful and popular...
so we're doing all it all again in 2027!!!
Gran Canaria Adventure Week
is back again for
January 2027
. We have some of what you've loved from previous years, plus new events and ideas to give you an even better winter sun experience.
Feedback from previous years:
"The socials were well organised and the group events were excellent"
"Loved the ability to do as much or as little as we wanted throughout the entire week"
"A fantastic event with something for everyone"
"Good range of activities to keep everyone happy, from leisure city tours to high octane hikes, canyoning, via ferrata - something for everyone! And the organisers are friendly and welcoming, feels like family which is nice"
"All the event leaders were great and super friendly and easy to talk to and ask questions"
Think you know Gran Canaria? Think again!
Let your next (or first!) visit to Gran Canaria be one filled with outdoor adventures. While the island is known as a year-round party destination for LGBTQ+ visitors, this trip is an opportunity to experience something different:
take part in outdoor activities; experience the beauty of the "real" Gran Canaria; and meet friends from around the world.
We are, once again, partnering with
CanCanaria
to bring you a full week of fun and adventurous activities. CanCanaria is a gay-owned and run company based on Gran Canaria, using their extensive local knowledge and the island's magnificent natural beauty to create a programme of excursions and trips that'll leave you with unforgettable memories and stories to tell. At the helm is former OutdoorLads' Chairman Patrick, so you know you will be in good and welcoming hands. Hiking, Climbing, Sailing, Surfing and Scuba Diving alongside tourist trips, socials, restaurants, bars, a pool party and boat trips.

Accommodation
Gran Canaria has accommodation to suit a variety of budgets, from basic self-catering apartments, to full service hotels and villas.
You are welcome to message the event leader or Patrick at CanCanaria for accommodation ideas, and to use the event page comments to arrange sharing. In due course we will also set up an OutdoorLads Telegram group too.
Flights & Transfers
Gran Canaria is easily accessible from various UK airports, with a flight time of around 4 hours. The transfer from the airport to Playa del Ingles is straight forward, either by public bus, taxi or pre-arranged holiday transfer service.

Title: An Evening with the Stars in Nottinghamshire
Summary:
We have secured a booking for a group visit to
Sherwood Observatory
.
Since its recent re-opening, the Observatory has been booked solid with group tours so we are pleased to offer this opportunity in Autumn 2026.
The visit promises a 90 minute adventure you'll never forget including a chance to ask anything you want to know about space and beyond. Additionally there will be:
a 20+ minute planetarium show and presentation by the expert team
a captivating talk in the lecture room that will spark your imagination
a thrilling opportunity to gaze at the stars and planets or our closest star, the Sun, depending on the season, (weather dependent)
a tour of the radio astronomy facilities
a visit of exhibition in the Science Centre to learn more about human space flight and the history of the Reservoir
Photos: Sherwood Observatory and used with permission
Difficulty & Distance: Sit and watch the stars go by. The site is broadly accessible but visiting the main telescope involves climbing some steps
